what: Analyse en composantes principales : des moyennes
title: Introduction à ggfacto : ACP, AC et ACM au plus près des données
text: Une ACP résume des variables numériques. Nous prenons les voitures de mtcars, décrites par six mesures actives ; le nombre de cylindres servira de variable supplémentaire. Le tableau s’ouvre sur ce que sont les variables avant l’analyse : moyenne, écart-type et coefficient de variation (sd/mean, l’écart-type en pourcentage de la moyenne, comparable d’une variable à l’autre malgré leurs unités). Viennent ensuite, axe par axe, la coordonnée de chaque variable (sa corrélation avec l’axe, colorée), sa contribution et sa qualité de représentation (cos2). Le premier axe (70 % de la variance) oppose la cylindrée, la puissance et le poids à la consommation (mpg) : c’est un facteur de taille. Le second oppose les voitures lentes à accélérer (qsec) aux autres. Le graphique superpose les voitures (en gris), les variables actives (les flèches) et les modalités supplémentaires, au barycentre de leurs voitures. Au survol, une flèche donne la moyenne et le coefficient de variation de sa variable ; une modalité supplémentaire, la moyenne de chaque variable active dans son groupe, colorée selon son écart à l’ensemble ; une voiture, ses valeurs. Le cercle des corrélations seul s’obtient avec ggfacto(acp, profiles = FALSE).
code: voitures <- mtcars |> mutate(cyl = factor(cyl))  acp <- principal_component_analysis(voitures, c(mpg, disp, hp, drat, wt, qsec)) interpret(acp) ggfacto(acp, voitures, sup_vars = cyl, interactive = TRUE)

what: Analyse des correspondances : un tableau croisé
title: Introduction à ggfacto : ACP, AC et ACM au plus près des données
text: Une AC est l’analyse d’un tableau croisé : la calcule donc sur le tableau lui-même. Nous croisons la religion et la préférence partisane de l’enquête américaine forcats::gss_cat, sans les non-réponses. color = "contrib" colore les cases selon leur contribution à la variance du tableau — celles qui pèsent dans l’analyse —, bleu pour une sur-représentation et rouge pour une sous-représentation. Pour chaque axe, interpret() ne garde que les modalités qui contribuent plus que la moyenne, face à face selon le signe de leur coordonnée. Le premier axe (76 % de la variance) oppose les protestant·es républicain·es aux personnes sans religion, indépendantes ou proches des démocrates ; le second, les juif·ves et les démocrates convaincu·es aux catholiques. Une fois les axes interprétés, les nomme : les noms s’impriment dans les graphiques et dans les tableaux. Au survol, chaque modalité affiche son profil : les pourcentages en ligne du tableau croisé, colorés selon l’écart à la moyenne. L’AC dessine la structure des écarts du tableau, sans rien dire de leur intensité : c’est le tableau coloré, à côté, qui la donne.
code: gss <- forcats::gss_cat |>   filter(!relig %in% c("No answer", "Don't know", "Not applicable"),          !partyid %in% c("No answer", "Don't know"))  tab(gss, relig, partyid, pct = "row", color = "contrib") ac <- correspondence_analysis(tab(gss, relig, partyid)) interpret(ac) ac <- name_axes(ac, "protestant·es républicain·es / sans religion",                     "catholiques / juif·ves démocrates") ggfacto(ac, interactive = TRUE)

what: Analyse des correspondances multiples : profils de réponses et tableau de Burt
title: Introduction à ggfacto : ACP, AC et ACM au plus près des données
text: Une ACM croise plusieurs questions à la fois. Nous prenons l’enquête tea de FactoMineR : 300 personnes, 18 questions actives sur leurs façons de boire le thé. En ACM, les taux de variance bruts sont faibles par construction : choisit le nombre d’axes à interpréter sur le taux modifié de Benzécri, dans le tableau des valeurs propres, ici 83 % sur les deux premiers axes. Le premier oppose le thé pris seulement à la maison au thé pris dehors, entre ami·es (salon de thé, restaurant, pub) ; le second, le thé en sachet acheté au supermarché au thé en vrac de boutique spécialisée. La base de données est redonnée en second argument, pour les variables supplémentaires (en italique). Deux choses se lisent au survol : les points gris sont les profils de réponses : les personnes qui ont donné exactement les mêmes réponses, leur taille disant leur nombre. Chacun affiche ses réponses ; chaque modalité affiche ses tableaux croisés avec toutes les autres questions actives : c’est le tableau de Burt sur lequel l’ACM est calculée, ses écarts à la moyenne colorés. revient ainsi aux données sans croiser les 18 questions deux à deux.
code: data(tea, package = "FactoMineR")  acm <- multiple_correspondence_analysis(tea, 1:18) interpret(acm, axes = 1:2) acm <- name_axes(acm, "à la maison / dehors, entre ami·es",                       "supermarché / boutique de thé") ggfacto(acm, tea, sup_vars = c(sex, SPC), interactive = TRUE)

title: Introduction à ggfacto : ACP, AC et ACM au plus près des données
text: La classification ascendante hiérarchique regroupe les individus les plus proches sur les premiers axes. Sans nb_clust, elle dessine l’arbre et coupe là où le gain de variance inter-classes chute.  Les classes s’écrivent dans la base avec mutate(), nommées dans l’ordre voulu ("nom" = numéro) : l’arbre n’est pas reconstruit. Le tableau décrit chaque classe par les variables actives, pondérées comme l’analyse, les écarts à l’ensemble colorés. Le graphique place les classes dans le nuage, leurs individus colorés :
code: hierarchical_clust(acm, ncp = 3) tea <- tea |>   mutate(classes = hierarchical_clust(acm, ncp = 3, names = c(     "Sachets du supermarché" = 1,     "Earl Grey sucré"        = 2,     "Earl Grey entre ami·es" = 4,     "Thé noir sans sucre"    = 5,     "Boutiques de thé"       = 3,     "Thé partout"            = 6   )))  clust_tab(acm, tea, classes) ggfacto(acm, tea, clust = classes)

title: Introduction à ggfacto : ACP, AC et ACM au plus près des données
text: Pondération : wt = dans les trois analyses ; les poids passent jusqu’aux tableaux des bulles d’information. ACM spécifique : excl = écarte des modalités (par défaut, les valeurs manquantes) ; sous-population : filter =, ou filter() dans le pipe, puis la base entière redonnée à ggfacto(). Graphiques : ce sont des ggplot, que l’complète avec + avant ggi() ; ggsave2() les enregistre ; ggmca_3d() et ggpca_3d() les dessinent en trois dimensions. Les coordonnées des individus s’ajoutent à la base avec mutate(axe1 = axis_coord(acm, 1)), comme les classes. La référence détaille chaque fonction.

title: Readable and Interactive Graph for Simple Correspondence Analysis — ggca
text: res.ca analysis made correspondence_analysis FactoMineR::CA. axes axes print, numeric vector length 2. show_sup Set FALSE leave supplementary rows columns . xlim, ylim Horizontal vertical axes limits, double vectors length 2. out_lims_move TRUE, levels outside xlim ylim moved edges graph rather left . type levels printed: "points" (coloured points names), "text" (coloured names) "labels" (coloured labels). text_repel default, labels moved overlap. Set FALSE print label exactly point. uppercase Print levels column variables ("col", default), row variables ("row"), none (NULL) uppercase. tooltips tooltips build: "row" profiles row levels, "col" column levels, default. rowtips_subtitle, coltips_subtitle, rowcolor_numbers, colcolor_numbers, filter Deprecated. tooltip headed variables' names; color_groups = "^.{2}" replaces rowcolor_numbers = 2, discard_levels replaces filter. cleannames Set TRUE clean levels names, removing prefix numbers like "1-", text parentheses. title title graph. text_size Size text. dist_labels type = "points", distance names points. right_margin margin right, cm. size_scale_max size largest point. default, computed spread levels' weights. use_theme default, specific ggplot2 theme used. Set FALSE customize theme. clust clusters levels one margin, hierarchical_clust returns outside mutate(): `clust = hierarchical_clust(res.ca, ncp = 2, nb_clust = 4)`. levels cluster take colour, cluster drawn barycentre. color_groups One colour per variable default. regex matched level name makes colour groups within variables ("^.{1}": upon first character). clust_color_groups Color groups clusters. keep_levels, discard_levels Regexes (vectors ) levels keep, leave . axes_names Names axes (just two selected ones), character vector. axes_reverse `1` invert left right, `2` invert , `1:2` . actives_in_bold Set active levels bold font. sup_in_italic Set supplementary levels italics. drawn black text. shift_colors Change colors variables. colornames_recode named character vector, forcats::fct_recode() style, rename colour groups (printed `options(ggfacto.verbose = TRUE)`). scale_color_light, scale_color_dark colours points names. get_data Returns data frames graph drawn , instead graph. lang NULL (session's language), "en" "fr".

title: The Graph of an Analysis — ggfacto

Hovering point shows data behind : level's crosstabs, coloured deviations mean, individual's answers values, supplementary level's percentages means. Supplementary variables clusters added data frame, MCA PCA, table, CA.

title: Readable and Interactive graph for multiple correspondence analysis — ggmca
text: res.mca object created multiple_correspondence_analysis FactoMineR::MCA. data data frame analysis made , find supplementary variables clusters: whole data frame, even analysis made subset multiple_correspondence_analysis. needed `sup_vars`, `clust` tooltip variables. sup_vars <tidy-select> supplementary variables draw, `tab()`: `sup_vars = c(SEXE, AGE)` (strings work ). need given analysis . active_tables coloured crosstabs shown tooltips. `"active"`, default, crosses active variable others: Burt table analysis computed , level edge cloud shows many colours one near centre . `"sup"` crosses supplementary variable active ones, `c("active", "sup")` , `NULL` none. Percentages coloured blue -represented red -represented, tabxplor::tab(color = "diff"). tooltip_vars_1lv <tidy-select> Variables whose first level (factor), weighted mean (number), added top tooltips. tooltip_vars <tidy-select> Variables whose levels added bottom tooltips. axes axes print, numeric vector length 2. axes_names Names axes (just two selected ones), character vector. axes_reverse Possibility reserve coordinates axes providing numeric vector : `1` invert left right ; `2` invert ; `1:2` invert . type Determines way sup_vars printed. "text" : colored text "points" : colored points text legends "labels" : colored labels "active_vars_only" : active levels alone, answer profiles "facets" : one graph profiles answer levels   first sup_vars (`profiles = TRUE` needed). different color used   . color_groups default, one color group levels `sup_vars`.  possible color `sup_vars` groups created upon levels, regex matched level name (groups printed console `options(ggfacto.verbose = TRUE)`). exemple, `color_groups = "^."`  makes groups upon first character  levels (uselful begin numbers).  color_groups = "^.{3}" upon first three characters.  color_groups = "NB.+$" takes anything `"NB"` end levels  names, etc. clust_color_groups Color groups `clust` variable (clusters). keep_levels regex, vector , matching supplementary levels keep: others discarded. discard_levels regex, vector , matching supplementary levels discard. cleannames Set TRUE clean levels names, removing prefix numbers like "1-", text parentheses. profiles default, answer profiles drawn back graph, light-grey points whose tooltips give answers active variables. clust, profile takes colour cluster, hover near one point lights points cluster. `FALSE` draws levels alone. profiles_tooltip_discard regex pattern remove useless levels among interactive tooltips profiles answers (ex. : levels expressing "" answers). clust variable `data` holding clusters, typically made hierarchical_clust, bare name (`clust = cah_culture`) string. clusters drawn supplementary variable, answer profiles one cluster coloured alike linked mouse hover (unless `profiles = FALSE`). max_profiles maximum number profiles points print, heaviest first. Default 2000. alpha_profiles alpha (transparency, 0 1) profiles answer. color_profiles default, clust provided, profiles colored based clust levels (HCPC clusters). Set FALSE avoid behaviour. can also give character vector levels `clust` variable . base_profiles_color base color answers profiles. Default gray. Set `NULL` discard profiles. `color_profiles`, set `NULL` discard non-colored profiles. text_repel default, labels moved overlap, ggrepel::geom_text_repel. Set FALSE print label exactly point, faster draw. title title graph. actives_in_bold Set `TRUE` set active variables bold font (sup variables plain). sup_in_italic Set supplementary levels italics, every graph package. `FALSE` sets upright. ellipses Set number 0 1 draw concentration ellipse level first sup_vars. 0.95 draw ellipses containing 95 individuals category. 0.5 draw median-ellipses, containing half individuals category. Every individual counts, whether `profiles = TRUE`. xlim, ylim Horizontal vertical axes limits, double vectors length 2. out_lims_move TRUE, levels xlim ylim removed, moved edges graph. shift_colors Change colors sup_vars points. colornames_recode named character vector fct_recode style rename colour groups. printed console `options(ggfacto.verbose = TRUE)`. scale_color_light scale color sup vars points scale_color_dark scale color sup vars texts text_size Size text. size_scale_max size largest point. default, computed spread weights points drawn, median answer profile stays visible. dist_labels type = points, distance labels points. right_margin margin right, cm. Useful read tooltips points placed right graph without formatting problems. use_theme default, specific ggplot2 theme used. Set FALSE customize theme. get_data Returns data frame create plot instead plot . lang NULL (session's language), "en" "fr": language tooltips axis titles. dat Deprecated former name `data`. Still accepted, warning; use `data` instead. cah, cah_color_groups Deprecated former names `clust` `clust_color_groups`. plot_data list data frames made ggmca_data.

what: Readable and Interactive Graph of the Individuals of a Principal Component Analysis — ggpca
title: Readable and Interactive Graph of the Individuals of a Principal Component Analysis — ggpca
text: biplot principal component analysis: cloud individuals plane two axes, levels supplementary variables barycentre individuals, clusters hierarchical_clust coloured, active variables arrows, circle correlations rescaled onto cloud. DIRECTION arrow reads : individual lies towards variables scores high ; length arrow distance arrow individual mean nothing, ggpca_cor_circle draws correlations scale. Hovering individual shows value active variable; hovering supplementary level shows mean active variable among individuals, coloured standardized difference population's (blue , red ), clust_tab . ggfacto draws principal component analysis, unless `profiles = FALSE` leaves nothing circle.

title: Readable and Interactive Graph of the Individuals of a Principal Component Analysis — ggpca

title: Readable and Interactive Graph of the Individuals of a Principal Component Analysis — ggpca
text: res.pca analysis made principal_component_analysis FactoMineR::PCA(). data data frame analysis made , find supplementary variables clusters: whole data frame, even analysis made subset . needed `sup_vars` `clust`. sup_vars <tidy-select> supplementary variables, `tab()`: level drawn weighted barycentre individuals. axes axes print, numeric vector length 2. axes_names Names axes (just two selected ones), character vector. axes_reverse Possibility reserve coordinates axes providing numeric vector : `1` invert left right ; `2` invert ; `1:2` invert . type Determines way sup_vars printed: "text", "labels", "points", "facets" (one graph individuals level first sup_vars). color_groups default, one color group levels `sup_vars`.  possible color `sup_vars` groups created upon levels, regex matched level name (groups printed console `options(ggfacto.verbose = TRUE)`). exemple, `color_groups = "^."`  makes groups upon first character  levels (uselful begin numbers).  color_groups = "^.{3}" upon first three characters.  color_groups = "NB.+$" takes anything `"NB"` end levels  names, etc. clust_color_groups Color groups `clust` variable (clusters). keep_levels regex, vector , matching supplementary levels keep: others discarded. discard_levels regex, vector , matching supplementary levels discard. cleannames Set TRUE clean levels names, removing prefix numbers like "1-", text parentheses. profiles default individuals drawn: `FALSE` draws supplementary levels variables alone. clust variable `data` holding clusters, typically made hierarchical_clust: individuals one cluster coloured alike linked mouse hover. max_profiles maximum number individuals draw: heaviest first, , among individuals equal weight, evenly spread sample. alpha_profiles alpha (transparency, 0 1) profiles answer. color_profiles default, clust provided, profiles colored based clust levels (HCPC clusters). Set FALSE avoid behaviour. can also give character vector levels `clust` variable . base_profiles_color base color answers profiles. Default gray. Set `NULL` discard profiles. `color_profiles`, set `NULL` discard non-colored profiles. text_repel default, labels moved overlap, ggrepel::geom_text_repel. Set FALSE print label exactly point, faster draw. title title graph. sup_in_italic Set supplementary levels italics, every graph package. `FALSE` sets upright. ellipses Set number 0 1 draw concentration ellipse level first sup_vars. 0.95 draw ellipses containing 95 individuals category. 0.5 draw median-ellipses, containing half individuals category. Every individual counts, whether `profiles = TRUE`. xlim, ylim Horizontal vertical axes limits, double vectors length 2. out_lims_move TRUE, levels xlim ylim removed, moved edges graph. shift_colors Change colors sup_vars points. colornames_recode named character vector fct_recode style rename colour groups. printed console `options(ggfacto.verbose = TRUE)`. scale_color_light scale color sup vars points scale_color_dark scale color sup vars texts text_size Size text. size_scale_max size largest point. default, computed spread weights points drawn, median answer profile stays visible. dist_labels type = points, distance labels points. right_margin margin right, cm. Useful read tooltips points placed right graph without formatting problems. use_theme default, specific ggplot2 theme used. Set FALSE customize theme. get_data Returns data frame create plot instead plot . lang NULL (session's language), "en" "fr": language tooltips axis titles. variables default active variables drawn arrows. Set `FALSE` draw individuals alone.

""       : 3D perspective Axes 1, 2, 3. type elements graph print, among : #' "var"         : initial variables axes, breaks "cor"         : normalized correlation vectors (length = 1) "cor_sphere"  : 3D sphere standard deviation 1 "ind"         : points individuals "ind_name"    : names individuals "main_plan"   : plan 1-2. title: Hierarchical Clustering on the Axes of an Analysis — hierarchical_clust
text: res analysis made multiple_correspondence_analysis, principal_component_analysis correspondence_analysis (FactoMineR::MCA(), PCA() CA(), GDAtools::speMCA() csMCA(), whose subcloud alone clustered). ncp number axes cluster : first ones, worth interpreting (see eigenvalues interpret). default: every axis, clustering follow noise. nb_clust number clusters. `-1`, default, tree cut gain -cluster inertia drops . Given `names`, number names. tree clustering tree drawn, choose number clusters? default, `nb_clust = -1`. leaves distinct points cloud: answer profiles multiple correspondence analysis, levels correspondence analysis. bar inertia gains carries number clusters makes, title share inertia `ncp` axes lies clusters drawn. consol k-means consolidation, moves individual nearest cluster tree cut. `TRUE`, default, FactoMineR::HCPC's k-means, counts every individual , weights . `"weighted"` counts weight (survey weights, level's count correspondence analysis) simpler k-means, Lloyd's, can place individuals differently even without weights. `FALSE` keeps clusters tree cuts . margin correspondence analysis, levels cluster: `"rows"`, default, `"columns"`. names names clusters, order levels take: either `c("Name 1", "Name 2", ...)`, clusters 1, 2, etc., `c("Name" = 2, "name" = 1, ...)`, forcats::fct_recode(). title: Multiple Correspondence Analysis — multiple_correspondence_analysis
text: data data frame. analyse subset population, give whole data frame `filter`, filter inside call native pipe, `data |> dplyr::filter(...) |> multiple_correspondence_analysis(...)`: analysis remembers rows used, ggmca, hierarchical_clust is_in_analysis can given whole data frame afterwards. active_vars <tidy-select> active variables. wt <tidy-select> weight variable, . excl levels exclude calculation axes (specific multiple correspondence analysis), matched exactly name. missing values active variable become level named `<VAR>.NA`, `NA`, default, excludes : `excl = NA` missing values , `excl = c(NA, "")` exclude level , `excl = "DIPLOMA.NA"` missing values one variable , `excl = NULL` keep every level. ncp number axes keep. default: eigenvalue table one chooses many axes interpret, truncated one show drop — also renormalises Benzecri's modified rate axes kept, axis gets different rate. cluster first axes, give hierarchical_clust `ncp`. graph default graph made, since result can plotted ggfacto. filter condition rows `data`, dplyr::filter(): rows `TRUE` analysed (`filter = AGE >= 18`). ... title: ggfacto 0.4.0
text: excl = takes exact level names; missing answers become <VAR>.NA levels, excluded default (specific MCA). filter = analyses subset; whole data frame passed every later function. clust =, names =, interactive =, lang =; options(ggfacto.widget_dir) writes widgets file documents. profiles = TRUE active_tables = "active" defaults: crosstables Burt table tooltips. MCA fitted distinct answer profiles (results, much faster); MCA2() keeps 0.3.2 fit individuals. missing value PCA sits variable’s weighted mean. Requires R >= 4.3, ggplot2 >= 4.0 tabxplor >= 2.0.1.
